---
title: "About MS-DIAL"
---

## Project Overview

MS-DIAL (Mass Spectrometry Data Independent AcquisitionaL software) is a comprehensive, free software for processing mass spectrometry data in metabolomics, lipidomics, and proteomics research.

### Mission

To provide the research community with a universal, user-friendly, and powerful tool for untargeted omics data analysis that supports multiple instruments, vendors, and analytical approaches.

## Development Team

MS-DIAL is developed and maintained by:

**RIKEN Center for Sustainable Resource Science (CSRS)**
- Systems Omics Laboratory
- Yokohama, Japan

### Principal Investigator

**Hiroshi Tsugawa, Ph.D.**
- Team Leader, RIKEN CSRS
- Project lead and main developer

### Contributors

The MS-DIAL project has benefited from contributions by numerous researchers, developers, and the global metabolomics community.

## History and Versions

### MS-DIAL 1.0 (2015)
- Initial release
- Focus on LC-MS/MS metabolomics
- DIA data processing

### MS-DIAL 2.0 (2016)
- Added GC-MS support
- Improved peak detection algorithms
- Enhanced spectral libraries

### MS-DIAL 3.0 (2018)
- Ion mobility support
- Imaging MS capabilities
- Multi-platform support

### MS-DIAL 4.0 (2020)
- Comprehensive lipidomics support
- In silico lipid databases
- LipidBlast integration
- Improved GUI

### MS-DIAL 5.0 (2022-Present)
- Major GUI overhaul
- Direct vendor format import
- Multi-database annotation
- Proteomics support
- Advanced fragmentation methods
- Enhanced performance

## Technology and Algorithms

MS-DIAL implements advanced algorithms for:

### Peak Detection
- Smoothing and baseline correction
- Peak picking in multiple dimensions
- Deconvolution of overlapping peaks

### Compound Identification
- Spectral similarity scoring
- Accurate mass matching
- Retention time/index alignment
- In silico fragmentation prediction

### Data Processing
- Multi-sample alignment
- Gap filling
- Normalization methods
- Statistical analysis (PCA)

### Databases
- MSP format spectral libraries
- In silico lipid databases
- Retention index libraries
- Custom database support

## Standards and Formats

MS-DIAL supports community standards:
- mzML (Proteomics Standards Initiative)
- MSP spectral format
- IUPAC lipid nomenclature
- MassBank spectral format
- GNPS molecular networking
